GNB.hook: The Bijagós archipelago off its coast is 88 islands, only about twenty of them inhabited — and a biosphere reserve.
GNB.place: A small Atlantic country tucked between Senegal and Guinea.
GNB.borders: Portuguese Guinea's limits against surrounding French West Africa, set by an 1886 Franco-Portuguese convention — rivers and short survey lines around the stretch of coast Portugal actually held.

GMB.hook: The smallest country in mainland Africa — a ribbon of land either side of one river, nowhere more than 50km wide.
GMB.place: Following the Gambia river inland, enclosed by Senegal on every side but the Atlantic.
GMB.borders: Africa's strangest border: a ribbon along both banks of the Gambia river, agreed with France in 1889 at roughly ten kilometres per bank — by legend, the range of British gunboat cannon.

CPV.hook: Ten volcanic islands that were completely uninhabited until Portuguese ships arrived in 1456 — everyone there descends from later arrivals.
CPV.place: An Atlantic archipelago about 570km west of Senegal, out on its own.
CPV.borders: Uninhabited Atlantic islands when the Portuguese arrived in 1456 — the state's extent is simply the archipelago Portugal settled; its only boundaries are maritime.

FRA.hook: Spans twelve time zones — more than any other country — because its overseas departments reach from the Pacific to the Caribbean to the Indian Ocean.
FRA.place: The hexagon between the Atlantic and the Alps, Spain beyond the Pyrenees, Germany across the Rhine.
FRA.borders: The 'natural frontiers' pursued for centuries: the Pyrenees crest fixed by the 1659 treaty with Spain, the Alpine line completed in 1860 when Nice and Savoy were annexed, and a flat northeastern edge that is simply where the wars stopped.

DEU.hook: Borders nine countries, more than any other in Europe — it touches nearly everyone from Denmark round to the Netherlands.
DEU.place: The middle of Europe, running from the North Sea coast down to the Alps.
DEU.borders: Cut to its present lines in 1945: the Oder and Neisse rivers became the Polish border — a quarter of prewar Germany lost — while the western edges are the old dynastic boundaries with France and the Low Countries, Alsace having changed hands four times in 75 years.

POL.hook: Holds Białowieża, the last great primeval lowland forest in Europe, and the wild bison that live in it.
POL.place: On the flat plain between Germany and the Baltics — the same corridor that runs unbroken from France to Russia.
POL.borders: Shifted bodily westward in 1945: Stalin kept everything east of the Bug river (roughly the 'Curzon line'), and Poland was compensated with German territory up to the Oder and Neisse rivers.

HUN.hook: Its language is related to nothing around it — the nearest relatives of Hungarian are Finnish and Estonian, 1,500km north.
HUN.place: The landlocked floor of the Carpathian basin, ringed by seven neighbours.
HUN.borders: The 1920 Treaty of Trianon cut the Kingdom of Hungary to a third of its size, drawing lines straight through the Hungarian-speaking plain — which is why Hungarian minorities sit just across every border.

CZE.hook: Drinks more beer per person than any other country, and has done for three decades running.
CZE.place: Landlocked west of Slovakia, wrapped on three sides by Germany, Poland and Austria.
CZE.borders: Bohemia's mountain rim — Sudetes, Ore Mountains, Šumava — is one of Europe's oldest stable borders, medieval in origin; the eastern line with Slovakia is just where the 1993 'Velvet Divorce' split Czechoslovakia.

NLD.hook: About a quarter of it lies below sea level, and much of that is land the Dutch built themselves by pumping the sea out.
NLD.place: The North Sea corner above Belgium and west of Germany.
NLD.borders: The 1839 treaty that let Belgium leave drew the line through Limburg and Brabant; the Baarle enclaves on that border — Belgian pockets inside Dutch pockets — survive from medieval lordship deals the treaty never untangled.

AUT.hook: Nearly two-thirds Alps, and Vienna is the only capital city with commercial vineyards inside its own boundaries.
AUT.place: Landlocked, the Alpine strip east of Switzerland and south of Germany.
AUT.borders: What was left of the Habsburg empire's Alpine, German-speaking core after the 1919 Treaty of Saint-Germain distributed the rest — the Brenner line handed South Tyrol's German speakers to Italy.

BEL.hook: Antwerp handles the large majority of the world's rough diamonds, in a district a few streets across.
BEL.place: The small country on the North Sea between France and the Netherlands.
BEL.borders: Drawn in 1839 when the great powers guaranteed a neutral buffer carved out of the Netherlands; the eastern cantons around Eupen were added from Germany in 1919, and the internal language line is older than the country.

CHE.hook: Landlocked and mountainous, yet its rivers drain to three different seas — the North Sea, the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.
CHE.place: The Alpine knot where France, Germany, Austria and Italy all meet.
CHE.borders: A confederation's accumulated medieval cantons frozen in place by the neutrality the powers guaranteed in 1815 — which is why the outline is a patchwork, with Italian-speaking Ticino hanging south of the Alps.

SVK.hook: Builds more cars per person than any country on Earth — roughly one for every five Slovaks each year.
SVK.place: Landlocked, directly east of Czechia. This is the one with Bratislava; Slovenia is 400km southwest.
SVK.borders: Trianon's 1920 lines made the southern edge — the Danube and a line through Hungarian-speaking country; the western edge is the amicable 1993 split of Czechoslovakia along the old Czech–Slovak provincial line.

SVN.hook: More than half forest, one of the greenest countries in Europe — and it has only about 47km of coast to its name.
SVN.place: At the head of the Adriatic below Austria. Not Slovakia, which is 400km northeast — the classic mix-up.
SVN.borders: Yugoslav republic lines turned international in 1991: the Karawanks crest with Austria from the 1919–20 treaties, the Italian edge from the postwar Trieste settlement, and a sliver of sea it had to win from Croatia in arbitration.

LUX.hook: The richest country per head on Earth, and nearly half its workforce drives in from France, Belgium and Germany every morning.
LUX.place: Tucked into the corner where Belgium, France and Germany meet.
LUX.borders: Partitioned three times as neighbours grew — the 1839 split alone gave the francophone west to Belgium — leaving today's rump grand duchy, kept alive because the powers wanted a buffer between France and Germany.

LIE.hook: Doubly landlocked — you must cross two borders to reach any sea — and it is the world's largest producer of false teeth.
LIE.place: A 25km sliver in the upper Rhine valley, entirely between Switzerland and Austria.
LIE.borders: Two medieval lordships the Liechtenstein family bought (1699, 1712) and never let be absorbed: the Rhine is the whole Swiss border, the Alpine ridge the Austrian one.

MCO.hook: The most densely populated country on Earth, and small enough to walk end to end in under an hour.
MCO.place: A 2km² notch on the French Riviera coast, close to the Italian border.
MCO.borders: A Grimaldi possession since 1297, shrunk to two square kilometres in 1861 when the family sold its hinterland towns of Menton and Roquebrune to France — the border is the edge of what they kept.

cityHooks.USA-washington-d-c: A diamond of land deliberately carved out of two states so no state could own the capital — the Potomac cuts the diamond's southwest edge.
cityHooks.USA-new-york: The harbor at the Hudson's mouth made it the front door of America — a fifth of all Americans can trace an ancestor through Ellis Island here.
cityHooks.USA-los-angeles: A desert coast with no natural harbor or river — the second-largest US city runs entirely on water piped hundreds of miles over mountains.
cityHooks.USA-chicago: Sits on the one low spot between the Great Lakes and the Mississippi basin — every railroad had to pass it, so it became the crossroads of the continent.
cityHooks.USA-miami: The only major US city conjured from a tropical swamp — it sits barely two meters above a rising sea, on the continent's southeastern tip.
cityHooks.CAN-ottawa: Chosen by Queen Victoria partly because it was a safe distance from the American border — unlike nearly every other Canadian city.
cityHooks.CAN-toronto: A third of Canadians live within a two-hour drive of it, all crowded onto Lake Ontario's northwest shore.
cityHooks.CAN-montreal: An island city in the St. Lawrence River, and the world's second-largest French-speaking city after Paris.
cityHooks.MEX-mexico-city: Built on a drained lake bed at 2,240m — the city is sinking up to half a meter a year into the old lake floor.
cityHooks.MEX-guadalajara: Mexico's second city, inland and west — the home of mariachi and, in the agave fields around it, tequila.
cityHooks.MEX-monterrey: Mexico's industrial powerhouse, tucked against the Sierra Madre just two hours' drive from the Texas border.
cityHooks.GTM-guatemala-city: Rebuilt on a plateau after earthquakes flattened the old capital Antigua — still ringed by three active volcanoes.
cityHooks.BLZ-belmopan: One of the world's tiniest capitals, built inland from scratch after Hurricane Hattie drowned coastal Belize City in 1961.
cityHooks.HND-tegucigalpa: A former silver-mining camp crammed into a mountain bowl — its airport approach between peaks was long rated the world's scariest.
cityHooks.SLV-san-salvador: Sits directly beneath its own volcano in the 'Valley of the Hammocks' — swung by earthquakes so often the nickname stuck.
cityHooks.NIC-managua: Placed on Lake Managua's shore as a compromise between feuding León and Granada — earthquakes leveled it twice, so its 'downtown' is still scattered.
cityHooks.CRI-san-jose: A coffee-boom capital on a mile-high plateau — the beans grown on the surrounding volcano slopes paid for its opera house.
cityHooks.PAN-panama-city: The only capital where you can watch ocean-going ships queue past skyscrapers — the Pacific mouth of the Canal is its front yard.
cityHooks.BRA-brasilia: Drawn in the shape of an airplane and built in under four years on empty savanna, to drag Brazil's center of gravity inland from the coast.
cityHooks.BRA-sao-paulo: The southern hemisphere's biggest city — a coffee fortune turned into an endless high-rise plateau just uphill from the sea.
cityHooks.BRA-rio-de-janeiro: Its bay was mistaken for a river mouth in January 1502 — hence 'January River' — and Sugarloaf mountain still guards the mistake.
cityHooks.BRA-belo-horizonte: Brazil's first planned city, ringed by the iron mountains of Minas Gerais that feed its steel mills.
cityHooks.BRA-porto-alegre: The industrial south's port, sitting where five rivers merge into a freshwater lagoon near Uruguay.
cityHooks.ARG-buenos-aires: Home to a third of all Argentines, on the bank of the Río de la Plata — a 'river' so wide the far shore in Uruguay is invisible.
cityHooks.COL-bogota: A capital at 2,640m on an Andean plateau — high enough that its climate is an eternal cool spring on the equator.
cityHooks.COL-medellin: Colombia's 'city of eternal spring', filling a narrow Andean valley — its cable cars are public transit up the slopes.
cityHooks.PER-lima: A capital in a desert that almost never rains — it drinks entirely from rivers falling out of the Andes behind it.
cityHooks.VEN-caracas: Squeezed into a mountain valley one ridge back from the Caribbean — its airport sits on the coast, a mountain pass away.
cityHooks.CHL-santiago: Backed by the highest Andes — from downtown you can ski at 3,000m and reach the Pacific, in opposite directions, within two hours.
cityHooks.BOL-sucre: The constitutional capital Bolivia keeps for its courts — government long since moved up to La Paz, 3,600m high.
cityHooks.ECU-quito: The closest capital to the equator line — the monument marking latitude zero stands in its northern suburbs.
cityHooks.PRY-asuncion: One of South America's oldest cities, the river port from which Buenos Aires itself was re-founded downstream.
cityHooks.URY-montevideo: Holds a third of Uruguay on the north shore of the Río de la Plata, staring across at Buenos Aires.
cityHooks.GBR-london: Built at the lowest point the Romans could bridge the Thames — the tide still reaches through the city twice a day.
cityHooks.FRA-paris: Began as a fort on an island in the Seine — every French road distance is still measured from the zero point outside Notre-Dame.
cityHooks.DEU-berlin: Sits far east in Germany — closer to Poland than to most of Germany's own big cities, a legacy of Prussia's eastern heart.
cityHooks.ITA-rome: The Tiber crossing where all roads converged — and the only capital with an entire sovereign state (the Vatican) inside it.
cityHooks.ESP-madrid: Europe's highest major capital, planted dead-center on Spain's plateau by royal decree — chosen precisely for being in the middle.
cityHooks.ESP-barcelona: Spain's Mediterranean door and Catalonia's capital — its street grid breaks into Gaudí's curves near the sea.
cityHooks.PRT-lisbon: Europe's westernmost capital, on the Tagus estuary — the earthquake that destroyed it in 1755 shook European philosophy too.
cityHooks.NLD-amsterdam: A city of 165 canals on wooden piles in a bog — the airport sits four meters below sea level.
cityHooks.GRC-athens: The Acropolis has been continuously in view for 3,400 years — the city fills the basin between it and the sea at Piraeus.
cityHooks.POL-warsaw: Rebuilt brick-by-brick from paintings after being 85% destroyed in 1944 — its 'old town' is a meticulous 1950s reconstruction.
cityHooks.UKR-kyiv: The thousand-year-old city on the Dnipro's bluffs where East Slavic civilization began — golden domes above a river highway.
cityHooks.RUS-moscow: The Kremlin is literally 'the fortress' — the city grew in concentric rings around it, and all Russian highways still radiate from it.
cityHooks.RUS-st-petersburg: Peter the Great's window on Europe, willed out of a Baltic swamp — its summer nights never fully darken.
cityHooks.TUR-ankara: Atatürk moved the capital here, deep in the Anatolian steppe, deliberately turning Turkey's back on imperial Istanbul.
cityHooks.TUR-istanbul: The only city on two continents — the Bosphorus through its middle is the strait between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.
cityHooks.CHN-beijing: The 'northern capital' — the Forbidden City at its heart aligns the whole street grid to the compass, as imperial cosmology demanded.
cityHooks.CHN-shanghai: At the mouth of the Yangtze, the river that drains a third of China — the world's busiest container port.
cityHooks.CHN-guangzhou: The Canton of the old trade — for centuries the single port where the West was allowed to buy from China.
cityHooks.CHN-shenzhen: A fishing town of 30,000 in 1980, a metropolis of 17 million now — the fastest city ever built, pressed against Hong Kong.
cityHooks.CHN-wuhan: The crossing where the Yangtze meets China's north–south railways — the country's central junction.
cityHooks.JPN-tokyo: The world's largest metropolis, on the Kanto plain — still officially a collection of villages that fused around Edo castle.
cityHooks.JPN-osaka: Japan's merchant capital and kitchen, on the Inland Sea — the historic rival to samurai Tokyo.
cityHooks.JPN-yokohama: The fishing village opened to foreign ships in 1859 — it grew into Japan's second city, fused to Tokyo's southern edge.
cityHooks.JPN-nagoya: The workshop between Tokyo and Osaka — Toyota's home turf on the Pacific coast's central bay.
cityHooks.KOR-seoul: Half of all South Koreans live in its metro area — barely 50km from the DMZ, within artillery range of the border.
cityHooks.KOR-busan: Korea's southern port, the last redoubt that never fell in the Korean War — now a container gateway facing Japan.
cityHooks.IND-new-delhi: The eighth city built on this site — imperial capitals stack here at the gap between the Thar desert and the Himalaya.
cityHooks.IND-mumbai: Seven islands stitched together by land reclamation — India's financial capital, film industry, and busiest port in one.
cityHooks.IND-kolkata: The British Raj's first capital, in the Ganges delta — the river here is already splitting into the world's largest delta.
cityHooks.IND-chennai: South India's gateway on the Bay of Bengal — the old Madras of the spice-and-cotton coast.
cityHooks.IDN-jakarta: Sinking so fast — up to 25cm a year — that Indonesia is building a replacement capital on Borneo.
cityHooks.THA-bangkok: Its full ceremonial name is 168 letters, a world record — the city sprawls across the Chao Phraya's delta marsh.
cityHooks.VNM-hanoi: The 'city between rivers' in the Red River delta — Vietnam's thousand-year-old northern capital.
cityHooks.VNM-ho-chi-minh-city: Still 'Saigon' to most of its residents — the Mekong delta's metropolis and the old southern capital.
cityHooks.MMR-yangon: The golden Shwedagon pagoda towers over it — Myanmar's generals abandoned it for a purpose-built capital in 2005.
cityHooks.PAK-karachi: Pakistan's port colossus on the Arabian Sea — it was the capital until Islamabad was purpose-built in the north.
cityHooks.PAK-lahore: The Mughal garden city, a stone's throw from the Indian border — the partition line of 1947 runs just east of it.
cityHooks.BGD-chattogram: Bangladesh's port on the Bay of Bengal, where much of the world's shipping goes to die on the breaking beaches nearby.
cityHooks.IRN-tehran: Climbs the slopes of the Alborz mountains — from downtown you look up at a 5,600m volcano between city and Caspian.
cityHooks.IRQ-baghdad: Founded as a perfect circle on the Tigris in 762 — for centuries the largest and most learned city on Earth.
cityHooks.ISR-jerusalem: A hilltop city sacred to three faiths — the walled Old City covers less than one square kilometer.
cityHooks.ISR-tel-aviv: Founded in 1909 on empty dunes north of ancient Jaffa — now Israel's Mediterranean business and beach capital.
cityHooks.SAU-riyadh: A mud-walled oasis town a century ago, now a desert metropolis dead-center in the peninsula.
cityHooks.SAU-jeddah: The Red Sea port that has received Mecca's pilgrims for thirteen centuries — the hajj gateway.
cityHooks.EGY-cairo: The largest city of Africa and the Arab world, pinned to the point where the Nile fans into its delta — pyramids stand in its suburbs.
cityHooks.EGY-alexandria: Alexander's harbor on the delta's western edge — its ancient lighthouse and library were both wonders of the world.
cityHooks.MAR-casablanca: Morocco's Atlantic port and business capital — far bigger than the four royal capitals, and younger than all of them.
cityHooks.NGA-abuja: Built in the 1980s at Nigeria's geographic center, a neutral capital between the Muslim north and Christian south.
cityHooks.NGA-lagos: Africa's largest city, spilling across lagoon islands — projected to be among the world's biggest megacities by 2100.
cityHooks.NGA-kano: The Sahel's ancient trading city — the southern terminus of trans-Saharan caravans for a thousand years.
cityHooks.ETH-addis-ababa: Africa's diplomatic capital at 2,355m — home of the African Union, in highlands cool enough for eucalyptus forests.
cityHooks.KEN-nairobi: Began as a railway supply depot in 1899 — the only capital with a national park (lions included) on its doorstep.
cityHooks.ZAF-pretoria: The executive capital in South Africa's three-capital split — administration here, parliament in Cape Town, courts in Bloemfontein.
cityHooks.ZAF-johannesburg: The world's largest city not on a river, coast, or lake — it exists purely because of the gold reef beneath it.
cityHooks.AUS-canberra: Sydney and Melbourne both refused to let the other be capital, so Australia built one in the bush between them.
cityHooks.AUS-sydney: Wrapped around the drowned river valley of Port Jackson — the harbor the First Fleet chose in 1788.
cityHooks.AUS-melbourne: Australia's southern rival, on Port Phillip Bay — a gold-rush boomtown that was briefly the richest city in the world.
cityHooks.NZL-wellington: The world's southernmost capital, gripping the hills of a strait so windy its nickname is simply 'Windy Wellington'.
